correctness.rationale: The count concerns the canonical algebraic-space quotient resolution K, not a deduction of arithmetic equivalence with the projective X₅. In the compatible choice of small resolution in Lemma 5.1, take the first two III factors to be u−v and u+v, the strict diagonal and graph blowups of Lemma 4.1; the remaining split node has invariant ruling ideals since negation changes both u,v signs and fixes c,d. Blowing up the last small exceptional line gives B with its lifted involution (Theorem 4.3 proof). At infinity Frobenius and negation reverse the same cycle, so their product fixes all 25 node pairs; over each the exceptional line is a k-form of P¹ and has six points. Type IV's conjugate components become split under the twist, and type III has two rational components. Independent field enumeration gave the Weierstrass counts 6,3,4,6,5,7, smooth twists 9,8,7, cubic counts 31/51 and split quadric counts 36/36. Together the twisted minimal fibres give 1196; corrections are 50+25·5+2·5+35, yielding 1416. The invariant ample-class Lefschetz isomorphism makes the H⁴ trace five times the H² trace; with the established vanishings and b₂(B)=43 this gives 215=43·5. Purity saturates the triangle inequality, fixing every eigenvalue, without asserting diagonalizability. Equivariant blowup passes this to the twisted H² of the small model and ordinary Frobenius has the same eigenvalues on its negation invariants. The five horizontal components and two explicitly defined exceptional fixed lines in Lemma 5.2 are each defined over k, so their seven H⁰(-1) contributions give 5. Tame quotient/blowup cohomology and the geometric dimensions give 31 copies of 5; duality gives 31 copies of 25 and yields the all-extension formula.
residual_risks: The elementary count check is conditional on the cited geometric models; it does not construct them. No Frobenius semisimplicity, arbitrary twist, or separate projective model comparison is asserted.

value.rationale: The complete zeta function is a natural arithmetic invariant of this specific Calabi–Yau quotient resolution. It separates the all-positive spectrum of K from the mixed-sign arithmetic of the parent, information not captured by their Betti dimensions. It gives all finite-extension counts, while the twisted trace explains the sign alignment rather than merely reporting one small-field count.
residual_risks: The invariant is attached to the canonical resolution in scope; no extra comparison of Frobenius actions on birational models is used.
